# Lab machinery: the estimator of the course, the specification menu, its
# validation, and the helpers of Tasks 3, 4 and 5 – check_score_file(),
# try_spec(), my_experiments(), submit_exploration(), prereg(), run_spec() and
# report_result(). The same code as R/spec_tools.R of the downloadable
# workspace, apart from the tag of the class chart, which lasts for the
# browser session here. Every specification is fitted live (about a second in
# the browser); data/spec_curve.csv places it among the 144, and
# data/menu_options.csv gives the reason for every option that is not on the
# curve. Both arrive with the page through its `resources:` list.

# ============================================================================
# CLASS CHART – the results Form, the course site and the tags
# ============================================================================
# The same block as in the helpers of the housing-audit case. The results Form
# that submit_exploration() and report_result() pre-fill: its ID and the entry
# codes of its seven fields. They belong to the Form that the cases of the
# course share, set up for the EU-frames case; a Form of its own replaces them
# here and nowhere else. The word in .case_word follows the tag in every label,
# so that the chart of this case reads only its own rows.
.form_id <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
.form_entry <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
                 t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
                 r = "entry.1660273001")
.case_word <- "cohabitation"
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/applied-replication"

# Both submissions of a participant carry one short tag inside the spec label,
# "explore: [amber-otter-42] cohabitation …", so that the participant can find
# their own marks on the class chart. The same functions sit in R/spec_tools.R
# of the workspace, which keeps the tag in a file; here it lasts for the
# browser session, and a nickname passed to either submission function sets it
# or brings it back after a reload.
.tag_words <- list(
  adj  = c("amber", "azure", "bright", "calm", "coral", "crisp", "dusky", "early",
           "fair", "gentle", "golden", "hazel", "ivory", "jade", "keen", "lively",
           "lunar", "misty", "noble", "olive", "pale", "quiet", "rapid", "rosy",
           "russet", "silver", "snowy", "solar", "sunny", "swift", "velvet", "vivid"),
  noun = c("otter", "heron", "lynx", "badger", "finch", "hare", "ibex", "kestrel",
           "lark", "marten", "newt", "owl", "puffin", "quail", "raven", "seal",
           "stoat", "tern", "vole", "wren", "bison", "crane", "dove", "egret",
           "fox", "gecko", "koala", "lemur", "moose", "panda", "robin", "swan")
)
.tag_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("tag", NULL, envir = .tag_env)

# A fresh tag, drawn without touching the random-number stream of the session.
.new_tag <- function() {
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit(if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
          else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(as.integer((as.numeric(Sys.time()) * 1000) %% 1e9) + Sys.getpid() %% 1e5)
  paste(sample(.tag_words$adj, 1), sample(.tag_words$noun, 1), sample(10:99, 1), sep = "-")
}

# A nickname reduced to lower-case ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens,
# at most 24 characters – the only form that the class chart parses.
.clean_tag <- function(x) {
  # iconv on Windows turns these into "?": the Romanian comma-below letters and the eszett
  x <- gsub("ß", "ss", chartr("ȘșȚț", "SsTt", trimws(as.character(x)[1])))
  ascii <- suppressWarnings(iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT"))
  if (!is.na(ascii)) x <- ascii
  x <- gsub("^-+|-+$", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x)))
  x <- gsub("-+$", "", substr(x, 1, 24))
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x))
    stop("A nickname needs at least one letter or digit, for example nickname = \"blue-heron\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  x
}

# The tag of this session: the nickname if one is given, otherwise the tag
# already drawn, otherwise a fresh one. Returns the tag and the one it replaced.
.class_tag <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  stored <- .tag_env$tag
  tag <- if (!is.null(nickname)) .clean_tag(nickname) else if (!is.null(stored)) stored else .new_tag()
  assign("tag", tag, envir = .tag_env)
  list(tag = tag, replaced = if (!is.null(stored) && !identical(tag, stored)) stored)
}

# ---- The estimator -------------------------------------------------------------
# A verbatim copy of R/cohabitation/_tools.R in the course repository,
# everything below its banner, which builds the curve; the downloadable
# workspace carries the same copy in R/spec_tools.R.

# The fits use base R (stats) and dplyr only, on purpose: the same code runs in
# the downloadable workspace and in webR on the browser lab. The multinomial
# model is fitted by Newton-Raphson below rather than by nnet, and the
# design-based errors are written out rather than taken from the survey
# package; R/cohabitation/check_parity.R checks both against nnet and survey.

# The menu of the curve, in menu order: every combination is one specification
# (2 x 2 x 3 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 144). Anything else is refused by check_spec() unless
# it is one of the off-curve options listed in OFF_CURVE.
SPEC_AXES <- list(
  cohorts = c("paper", "five_years"),
  horizon = c("five_years", "three_years"),
  adjust  = c("none", "age", "composition"),
  weights = c("weighted", "unweighted"),
  time    = c("linear", "yearly"),
  model   = c("mlogit", "logit", "cloglog")
)

# Options that fit_spec() can also fit off the curve, for the displays and the
# reference marks. For `comparison`, `education`, `short` and `errors` the first
# option is the one that the curve holds fixed.
OFF_CURVE <- list(
  adjust     = c("race_period", "educ_period", "total_duration"),
  time       = c("none"),
  model      = c("lpm"),
  comparison = c("1995_2006", "2002_2006", "1995_2011", "2002_2011", "2006_2011"),
  education  = c("paper", "score"),
  short      = c("drop", "keep"),
  errors     = c("design", "woman", "model")
)

# The surveys compared: the earlier and the later cohort. The paper compares
# NSFG 1995 with NSFG 2006-2010; the others pair the cycles that SCORE and the
# Multi100 analysts used, and `2011` pools NSFG 2011-2013 and 2013-2015, as
# the SCORE replication did.
COMPARISONS <- list(
  "1995_2006" = list(earlier = "1995", later = "2006-10"),
  "2002_2006" = list(earlier = "2002", later = "2006-10"),
  "1995_2011" = list(earlier = "1995", later = c("2011-13", "2013-15")),
  "2002_2011" = list(earlier = "2002", later = c("2011-13", "2013-15")),
  "2006_2011" = list(earlier = "2006-10", later = c("2011-13", "2013-15"))
)

# Covariates of each adjustment set besides the later cohort (`later`) and the
# duration terms. `race_period` is Model 2 of Table 2 of the paper and
# `educ_period` its Model 1: with the interactions, the coefficient of `later`
# is the change for non-Hispanic white women or for college graduates only.
# `total_duration` adds the length of the whole union, a quantity that is known
# only once the union has ended, as the file that SCORE built does.
ADJUST_TERMS <- list(
  none           = character(0),
  age            = c("age", "age2"),
  composition    = c("age", "age2", "black", "hispanic", "other", "less_hs", "hs", "some_college"),
  race_period    = c("age", "age2", "black", "hispanic", "other", "less_hs", "hs", "some_college",
                     "later_black", "later_hispanic", "later_other"),
  educ_period    = c("age", "age2", "black", "hispanic", "other", "less_hs", "hs", "some_college",
                     "later_less_hs", "later_hs", "later_some_college"),
  total_duration = c("age", "age2", "black", "hispanic", "other", "less_hs", "hs", "some_college",
                     "union_length")
)

# The specification closest to the model of the paper (Table 2), without its
# interaction of race-ethnicity and period
REFERENCE <- list(cohorts = "paper", horizon = "five_years", adjust = "composition",
                  weights = "weighted", time = "linear", model = "mlogit")

check_spec <- function(cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model,
                       comparison = "1995_2006", education = "paper", short = "drop", errors = "design") {
  chosen <- list(cohorts = cohorts, horizon = horizon, adjust = adjust, weights = weights, time = time,
                 model = model, comparison = comparison, education = education, short = short,
                 errors = errors)
  widened <- intersect(names(SPEC_AXES), names(OFF_CURVE))
  allowed <- c(purrr::imap(SPEC_AXES, \(options, axis) c(options, OFF_CURVE[[axis]])),
               OFF_CURVE[setdiff(names(OFF_CURVE), widened)])
  bad <- names(chosen)[!purrr::map2_lgl(chosen, allowed[names(chosen)], \(v, ok) length(v) == 1 && v %in% ok)]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("Not on the menu: ", paste0(bad, " = '", unlist(chosen[bad]), "'", collapse = ", "),
         ". The options are listed in menu_options.csv.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# The unions of a specification: first premarital cohabitations of NSFG 1995
# (begun 1990-1995) against those of NSFG 2006-2010, begun no more than five
# years before the interview; `paper` keeps from NSFG 2006-2010 only the
# unions begun in 2005 or later, as the paper does. Unions that lasted less
# than a month are left out unless `short = "keep"`. `later` marks the later
# cohort.
spec_unions <- function(unions, cohorts = "paper", short = "drop", comparison = "1995_2006") {
  pair <- COMPARISONS[[comparison]]
  unions |>
    dplyr::filter(cycle %in% c(pair$earlier, pair$later), since_start <= 60, !is.na(duration),
                  .env$short == "keep" | duration >= 1,
                  .env$cohorts == "five_years" | cycle != "2006-10" | from_2005) |>
    dplyr::mutate(later = as.integer(cycle %in% pair$later))
}

# One row per union and month at risk, from the month in which the couple
# moved in (month 1) to the month of the marriage, the separation or the
# interview; the outcome is recorded in the last month. Under a three-year
# horizon months after the 36th are dropped and a union still intact at 36
# months counts as intact.
person_months <- function(unions, horizon = "five_years") {
  last <- if (horizon == "three_years") 36 else Inf
  unions |>
    dplyr::mutate(n_months = pmin(duration + 1, last),
                  event = dplyr::if_else(duration + 1 <= last, outcome, "intact")) |>
    tidyr::uncount(n_months, .id = "month") |>
    dplyr::mutate(y = dplyr::if_else(month == duration + 1, event, "intact")) |>
    dplyr::select(-event)
}

# The analysed person-months of one specification with every column that a
# model of the menu can use
spec_frame <- function(unions, cohorts = "paper", horizon = "five_years", weights = "weighted",
                       comparison = "1995_2006", education = "paper", short = "drop") {
  spec_unions(unions, cohorts, short, comparison) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      educ = if (.env$education == "score") educ_score else educ,
      age = age_start, age2 = age_start^2,
      black = as.integer(race == "black"), hispanic = as.integer(race == "hispanic"),
      other = as.integer(race == "other"),
      less_hs = as.integer(educ == "less_hs"), hs = as.integer(educ == "hs"),
      some_college = as.integer(educ == "some_college"),
      later_black = later * black, later_hispanic = later * hispanic, later_other = later * other,
      later_less_hs = later * less_hs, later_hs = later * hs, later_some_college = later * some_college,
      union_length = duration,
      w = if (.env$weights == "weighted") weight else 1
    ) |>
    person_months(horizon) |>
    dplyr::mutate(w = w / mean(w),
                  year_of_union = pmin(ceiling(month / 12), 5))
}

# The design matrix: an intercept, the later cohort, the adjustment terms and
# the duration terms (months since the start, or one baseline per year of the
# union with the first year as reference)
spec_matrix <- function(frame, adjust = "composition", time = "linear") {
  x <- cbind(`(Intercept)` = 1, later = frame$later, as.matrix(frame[, ADJUST_TERMS[[adjust]]]))
  if (time == "linear") x <- cbind(x, month = frame$month)
  if (time == "yearly") {
    years <- sort(unique(frame$year_of_union))[-1]
    yr <- outer(frame$year_of_union, years, `==`) * 1
    colnames(yr) <- paste0("year", years)
    x <- cbind(x, yr)
  }
  x
}

# Multinomial logit by Newton-Raphson, with intact as the reference category:
# one column of coefficients for marriage and one for separation. Returns the
# coefficients, the information matrix and the score contribution of every row.
fit_mlogit <- function(x, y, w, tol = 1e-10, max_iter = 50) {
  yy <- cbind(marriage = as.numeric(y == "marriage"), separation = as.numeric(y == "separation"))
  k <- ncol(x)
  # Start from the shares of the three outcomes, with the intercept in column 1
  beta <- matrix(0, k, 2)
  beta[1, ] <- log(colSums(w * yy) / sum(w * (1 - rowSums(yy))))  # r-style: keep – a coefficient matrix
  probs <- function(beta) {
    e <- exp(x %*% beta)
    e / (1 + rowSums(e))
  }
  info_of <- function(p) {
    block <- \(a, b) crossprod(x, x * (w * (p[, a] * (a == b) - p[, a] * p[, b])))
    rbind(cbind(block(1, 1), block(1, 2)), cbind(block(2, 1), block(2, 2)))  # r-style: keep – matrix blocks
  }
  loglik <- function(beta) {
    eta <- x %*% beta
    sum(w * (rowSums(yy * eta) - log(1 + rowSums(exp(eta)))))
  }
  ll <- loglik(beta)
  for (iter in seq_len(max_iter)) {  # r-style: keep – Newton-Raphson, each step needs the last
    p <- probs(beta)
    grad <- c(crossprod(x, w * (yy[, 1] - p[, 1])), crossprod(x, w * (yy[, 2] - p[, 2])))
    step <- matrix(solve(info_of(p), grad), k, 2)
    # Halve the step until the log-likelihood does not fall
    halvings <- purrr::detect_index(0:20, \(h) loglik(beta + step / 2^h) >= ll)
    beta_new <- beta + step / 2^(max(halvings, 1) - 1)
    ll_new <- loglik(beta_new)
    beta <- beta_new
    if (abs(ll_new - ll) < tol * (abs(ll) + tol)) break
    ll <- ll_new
  }
  p <- probs(beta)
  dimnames(beta) <- list(colnames(x), colnames(yy))
  scores <- cbind(x * (w * (yy[, 1] - p[, 1])), x * (w * (yy[, 2] - p[, 2])))
  list(coef = beta, info = info_of(p), scores = scores, p_marriage = p[, 1], iter = iter)
}

# A binary model of marriage in the month (a separation month counts as a month
# without marriage, after which the union leaves the risk set): logit or
# complementary log-log by glm, or the linear probability model by lm. Returns
# what fit_mlogit() returns, for the marriage column only.
fit_binary <- function(x, y, w, model) {
  ym <- as.numeric(y == "marriage")
  if (model == "lpm") {
    fit <- stats::lm.wfit(x, ym, w)
    e <- ym - drop(x %*% fit$coefficients)
    info <- crossprod(x, x * w)
    return(list(coef = cbind(marriage = fit$coefficients), info = info, scores = x * (w * e),
                residual_var = sum(w * e^2) / (length(ym) - ncol(x))))
  }
  fam <- stats::quasibinomial(link = if (model == "logit") "logit" else "cloglog")
  fit <- stats::glm.fit(x, ym, weights = w, family = fam)
  eta <- drop(x %*% fit$coefficients)
  mu <- fam$linkinv(eta)
  d <- fam$mu.eta(eta)
  info <- crossprod(x, x * (w * d^2 / fam$variance(mu)))
  list(coef = cbind(marriage = fit$coefficients), info = info,
       scores = x * (w * d * (ym - mu) / fam$variance(mu)), p_marriage = mu)
}

# Between-cluster variance of summed score contributions, clusters within
# strata: the Taylor linearisation of the survey package with its default
# with-replacement design. `design` lists every cluster of the surveys with
# its stratum; clusters that hold no analysed row enter with zero totals, as
# they do for a subset of a survey design. Clustering by woman passes the women
# as clusters of a single stratum.
meat_clustered <- function(scores, cluster, design) {
  totals <- rowsum(scores, cluster, reorder = FALSE)
  empty <- setdiff(design$psu, rownames(totals))
  totals <- rbind(totals, matrix(0, length(empty), ncol(scores), dimnames = list(empty, NULL)))  # r-style: keep – matrices
  str_of <- design$stratum[match(rownames(totals), design$psu)]
  n_h <- as.vector(table(str_of)[str_of])
  means <- rowsum(totals, str_of, reorder = FALSE)[str_of, , drop = FALSE] / n_h
  crossprod((totals - means) * sqrt(n_h / (n_h - 1)))
}

# Any model of the menu with every coefficient: the coefficients (one column per
# equation: marriage, and separation for the multinomial model), their
# variance under the chosen errors and under the model, and the degrees of
# freedom and counts of the fit. Design-based errors take the strata and
# clusters of the two surveys, with t on clusters minus strata minus
# coefficients plus one df, as svyglm counts them.
fit_model <- function(unions, cohorts = "paper", horizon = "five_years", adjust = "composition",
                      weights = "weighted", time = "linear", model = "mlogit", comparison = "1995_2006",
                      education = "paper", short = "drop", errors = "design") {
  check_spec(cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model, comparison, education, short, errors)
  frame <- spec_frame(unions, cohorts, horizon, weights, comparison, education, short)
  x <- spec_matrix(frame, adjust, time)
  # Columns are divided by their largest value for the fit (age squared runs to
  # about 1,800), which keeps the information matrix well conditioned; the
  # results are scaled back below.
  col_scale <- apply(abs(x), 2, max)  # r-style: keep – a model matrix, not a data frame
  xs <- sweep(x, 2, col_scale, `/`)
  fit <- if (model == "mlogit") fit_mlogit(xs, frame$y, frame$w) else fit_binary(xs, frame$y, frame$w, model)
  bread <- solve(fit$info)

  design <- unions |>
    dplyr::filter(cycle %in% frame$cycle) |>
    dplyr::distinct(stratum, psu)
  women <- unique(paste(frame$cycle, frame$caseid))
  meat <- switch(errors,
                 design = meat_clustered(fit$scores, frame$psu, design),
                 woman = meat_clustered(fit$scores, paste(frame$cycle, frame$caseid),
                                        data.frame(stratum = "all", psu = women)),
                 model = NULL)
  v <- if (is.null(meat)) bread else bread %*% meat %*% bread
  bread_model <- if (model == "lpm") bread * fit$residual_var else bread
  scale_all <- rep(col_scale, ncol(fit$coef))
  terms <- paste(rep(colnames(fit$coef), each = ncol(x)), colnames(x), sep = ":")
  unscale <- \(m) structure(m / outer(scale_all, scale_all), dimnames = list(terms, terms))

  list(
    coef = fit$coef / col_scale, vcov = unscale(v), vcov_model = unscale(bread_model),
    df = switch(errors,
                design = length(unique(frame$psu)) - length(unique(frame$stratum)) - length(fit$coef) + 1,
                woman = length(women) - 1,
                model = Inf),
    n = nrow(frame), n_unions = length(women), n_marriages = sum(frame$y == "marriage"),
    n_psu = length(unique(frame$psu)), n_strata = length(unique(frame$stratum))
  )
}

# One specification: the coefficient of the later cohort in the marriage
# equation (log odds of marrying in a month for logit, log of the relative risk
# of marrying rather than staying together for the multinomial model, log of
# the monthly hazard for the complementary log-log; negative = cohabitors of
# the later cohort marry less, the direction of the claim), its error and test
# under the chosen errors (design-based on the curve), the conventional test,
# and the partial correlation by the Multi100 rule from the conventional z and
# the number of person-months.
fit_spec <- function(unions, cohorts = "paper", horizon = "five_years", adjust = "composition",
                     weights = "weighted", time = "linear", model = "mlogit", comparison = "1995_2006",
                     education = "paper", short = "drop", errors = "design") {
  m <- fit_model(unions, cohorts, horizon, adjust, weights, time, model, comparison, education, short, errors)
  b <- m$coef["later", "marriage"]
  se <- sqrt(m$vcov["marriage:later", "marriage:later"])
  stat <- b / se
  se_model <- sqrt(m$vcov_model["marriage:later", "marriage:later"])
  z_model <- b / se_model
  data.frame(
    cohorts = cohorts, horizon = horizon, adjust = adjust, weights = weights, time = time, model = model,
    comparison = comparison, education = education, short = short, errors = errors,
    b = b, se = se, stat_type = if (is.finite(m$df)) "t" else "z", stat = stat, df = m$df,
    p = 2 * stats::pt(-abs(stat), m$df),
    se_model = se_model, z_model = z_model, p_model = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(z_model)),
    r = r_multi100(z_model, "z", NA, m$n),
    ratio = exp(b),
    n = m$n, n_unions = m$n_unions, n_marriages = m$n_marriages, n_psu = m$n_psu, n_strata = m$n_strata
  )
}

# The conversion rules of Multi100 (standard_correlation_coefficient.R): t with
# its df; z with the sample size standing in for the missing df; F with one
# numerator df read as the square of a t; a chi-square read as the square of a
# z, so it carries no sign.
r_multi100 <- function(stat, stat_type, df, n) {
  stat_type <- rep_len(stat_type, length(stat))
  dplyr::case_when(
    stat_type == "t" ~ stat / sqrt(stat^2 + df),
    stat_type == "z" ~ tanh(abs(stat) * sqrt(1 / (n - 3))) * sign(stat),
    stat_type == "F" ~ sqrt(abs(stat) / (abs(stat) + df)),
    stat_type == "chi2" ~ tanh(sqrt(abs(stat)) * sqrt(1 / (n - 3)))
  )
}

# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices() reads the fifteen
# my_* choices of the preregistration cell. An option that is not on the
# curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the page of the course
# site that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve.
.on_menu <- function(axis, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[axis]]

.refuse <- function(axis, v, as_args) {
  shown <- if (as_args) axis else paste0("my_", axis)
  keep  <- .menu[[axis]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("cases/cohabitation/map.qmd"))
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".", shown, shown, keep[1]),
         call. = FALSE)
  opts <- .options()
  row  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, .data$option == .env$v)
  off  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, !.data$on_curve)$option
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of %d specifications, so it has no result here.",
            shown, v, row$label, nrow(.curve())),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown, .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown, v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(keep, collapse = " | ")),
    if (length(off) > 0)
      sprintf("  Off the curve, refused with the reason why: %s.", paste(off, collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

# ---- The live fit ----------------------------------------------------------------
# fit_spec() on the six decisions that vary on the curve, with the 95%
# interval of the estimate (t on the design-based df) and the place of the
# result among the 144. The fit is checked against its row of
# data/spec_curve.csv; a difference means that the page loaded an incomplete
# file.
.result <- function(ch) {
  fit <- fit_spec(.unions(), ch$cohorts, ch$horizon, ch$adjust, ch$weights, ch$time, ch$model) |>
    as.list()
  crit <- stats::qt(0.975, fit$df)
  curve <- .curve()
  stored <- dplyr::filter(curve, .data$cohorts == ch$cohorts, .data$horizon == ch$horizon,
                          .data$adjust == ch$adjust, .data$weights == ch$weights,
                          .data$time == ch$time, .data$model == ch$model)
  if (nrow(stored) != 1) {
    warning("This specification has no row in data/spec_curve.csv; reload the page.",
            call. = FALSE)
  } else if (abs(fit$b - stored$b) > 1e-6 || abs(fit$stat - stored$stat) > 1e-6) {
    warning(sprintf("The live fit (b = %.5f, t = %.3f) differs from the curve that this page loaded (b = %.5f, t = %.3f). Reload the page.",
                    fit$b, fit$stat, stored$b, stored$stat),
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  c(fit, list(ci_low = fit$b - crit * fit$se, ci_high = fit$b + crit * fit$se,
              further = sum(curve$b < fit$b - 1e-9), n_curve = nrow(curve)))
}

.class_line <- function(res) {
  below <- res$b < 0
  sig   <- res$p < 0.05
  if (below && sig) "below zero and significant at 5%, in the direction of the claim"
  else if (below) "below zero, but not significant at 5%"
  else if (sig) "above zero and significant at 5%, against the direction of the claim"
  else "above zero and not significant at 5%"
}

## Task 2, continued – The estimand and the graph {#task-2-estimand-and-graph}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template that you can adapt [@LundbergEtAl2021WhatYourEstimand]:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is, for each cohabiting union, in each month in which it is still intact, whether the couple marries in that month. The **target population** is the first cohabitations that came before any marriage, of women aged 15–44 in the United States. The estimand compares the average of that quantity in unions begun in 2005–2010 with unions begun in 1990–1995, either as the two cohorts were or for women of the same age at the start, race-ethnicity and education.

There is a catch in the last clause. Nobody can assign the period in which a union begins, so this is a comparison of two populations of unions rather than of one union under two conditions, and whether the change in who cohabits belongs to the answer is a decision. A causal graph sets this out. A graph of this kind is a diagram of what causes what: variables are nodes, arrows run from cause to effect, and the rules for reading the graph say which paths between the period and marriage are open, given what the comparison holds constant. The graph below is written in ordinary R, one arrow per string, each written the way it is drawn: `"education -> marriage"` is the arrow from education to the chance that a cohabiting couple marries. Education and race-ethnicity shape both whether a woman cohabits at all (`cohabits`) and whether a cohabiting couple marries; the age at which the couple moved in (`age_start`) shapes marriage too; and the period shapes who cohabits, because cohabitation spread. One arrow is switched off with a `#`: the arrow from the period to marriage, which is the change that the claim is about.


::: {.cell autorun='true'}
```{webr}

#| autorun: true

# adjustmentSets() returns the minimal adjustment sets for the total effect,
# isAdjustmentSet() checks one set, paths() lists the paths between two nodes
# and whether each is open given a conditioning set Z, and plot_dag() draws
# the graph with ggplot2. They agree with dagitty on every graph of this
# task, and plot_dag() also draws a graph that dagitty built.

# Where each node sits in the figure, with y counted upwards: the period on
# the left, marriage on the right, the characteristics of the woman above the
# line between them and the selection into cohabitation below it. A node
# without a position here is drawn on a row below the graph.
.dag_xy <- list(period = c(0, 0), marriage = c(4, 0), race = c(1.2, 1.6),
                education = c(2.6, 1.8), age_start = c(3.6, 1.1), cohabits = c(2, -1.4))
dag_engine <- "built-in"

.make_dag_builtin <- function(..., exposure, outcome, latent) {
  arrows <- c(...)
  edges <- purrr::map(arrows, \(a) {
    ends <- trimws(strsplit(a, "->", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
    if (length(ends) < 2 || !all(nzchar(ends)) || grepl("<-", a, fixed = TRUE))
      stop(sprintf("Write each arrow as \"cause -> effect\", for example \"education -> marriage\"; \"%s\" is not one.",
                   a), call. = FALSE)
    data.frame(from = ends[-length(ends)], to = ends[-1])
  }) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |>
    dplyr::distinct()
  structure(list(edges = edges, nodes = unique(c(exposure, outcome, edges$from, edges$to)),
                 exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome, latent = latent),
            class = "simple_dag")
}

# The same graph as a dagitty object, as R/dag_starter.R of the workspace
# builds it; dagitty counts y downwards, so the heights change sign.
.make_dag_dagitty <- function(..., exposure, outcome, latent) {
  arrows <- c(...)
  nodes <- unique(c(exposure, outcome, trimws(unlist(strsplit(arrows, "->|<-")))))
  declare <- purrr::map_chr(nodes, \(v) {
    tags <- c(if (v %in% exposure) "exposure",
              if (v %in% outcome) "outcome",
              if (v %in% latent) "latent",
              if (v %in% names(.dag_xy))
                sprintf("pos=\"%s,%s\"", .dag_xy[[v]][1], -.dag_xy[[v]][2]))
    if (length(tags) == 0) v else sprintf("%s [%s]", v, paste(tags, collapse = ","))
  })
  dagitty::dagitty(paste0("dag {\n", paste(c(declare, arrows), collapse = "\n"), "\n}"))
}

# A graph from arrows written "cause -> effect", one per string. The named
# arguments come last, so that switching off the last arrow with a # never
# leaves a comma dangling.
make_dag <- function(..., exposure = "period", outcome = "marriage", latent = character(0)) {
  build <- if (identical(dag_engine, "dagitty")) .make_dag_dagitty else .make_dag_builtin
  build(..., exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome, latent = latent)
}

.dag_has_edge <- function(dag, a, b) any(dag$edges$from == a & dag$edges$to == b)

# A node counts as one of its own descendants, which is what the collider rule
# below needs.
.dag_descendants <- function(dag, v) {
  kids <- setdiff(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from %in% v], v)
  if (length(kids) == 0) v else .dag_descendants(dag, union(v, kids))
}

# Every simple path between two nodes, ignoring the direction of the arrows.
# The recursion is safe only because a teaching graph is tiny.
.dag_paths <- function(dag, from, to) {
  neighbours <- \(v) unique(c(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from == v], dag$edges$from[dag$edges$to == v]))
  extend <- function(path) {
    v <- path[length(path)]
    if (v == to) return(list(path))
    purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(setdiff(neighbours(v), path), \(w) extend(c(path, w))))
  }
  extend(from)
}

# A path is blocked by the set z if any node along it is either a non-collider
# inside z, or a collider with no descendant in z.
.dag_path_blocked <- function(dag, path, z) {
  if (length(path) < 3L) return(FALSE)
  purrr::some(seq(2L, length(path) - 1L), \(i) {
    node <- path[i]
    collider <- .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i - 1L], node) && .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i + 1L], node)
    if (collider) !any(.dag_descendants(dag, node) %in% z) else node %in% z
  })
}

# The backdoor criterion: a set qualifies if it holds no descendant of the
# exposure and blocks every path that starts with an arrow into the exposure.
.closes_backdoors <- function(x, z, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome) {
  backdoor <- purrr::keep(.dag_paths(x, exposure, outcome), \(p) .dag_has_edge(x, p[2L], exposure))
  !any(z %in% .dag_descendants(x, exposure)) &&
    purrr::every(backdoor, \(p) .dag_path_blocked(x, p, z))
}

# Brute-forced over subsets of the observed variables that are not
# descendants of the exposure: smallest sets first, and a set is skipped once
# it contains a set already found, which leaves the minimal ones.
.adjustment_sets_builtin <- function(x, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome,
                                     effect = "total", ...) {
  if (!identical(effect, "total"))
    stop("The graph code built into this page answers the total effect only; paths() shows what a conditioning set opens and closes.",
         call. = FALSE)
  candidates <- setdiff(x$nodes, c(outcome, x$latent, .dag_descendants(x, exposure)))
  subsets <- c(list(character(0)),
               purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(seq_along(candidates),
                                              \(k) utils::combn(candidates, k, simplify = FALSE))))
  closing <- purrr::keep(subsets, \(z) .closes_backdoors(x, z, exposure, outcome))
  minimal <- purrr::reduce(closing, \(found, z)
    if (purrr::some(found, \(f) all(f %in% z))) found else c(found, list(sort(z))), .init = list())
  structure(minimal, class = "simple_dag_sets")
}

print.simple_dag_sets <- function(x, ...) {
  shown <- if (length(x) == 0) "(no set of observed variables closes every backdoor path)" else
    purrr::map_chr(x, \(z) if (length(z) > 0) paste0("{ ", paste(z, collapse = ", "), " }") else "{}")
  writeLines(shown)
  invisible(x)
}

# Registered rather than left in the session: these cells do not evaluate in
# the global environment, so plain S3 dispatch would not find the method.
registerS3method("print", "simple_dag_sets", print.simple_dag_sets)

.is_adjustment_set_builtin <- function(x, Z, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome, ...) {
  .closes_backdoors(x, Z, exposure, outcome)
}

# The paths between two nodes, each with its arrows, and whether it is open
# given the conditioning set Z; sorted as dagitty sorts them.
.paths_builtin <- function(x, from = x$exposure, to = x$outcome, Z = character(0), ...) {
  found <- .dag_paths(x, from, to)
  label <- purrr::map_chr(found, \(p) {
    steps <- purrr::map_chr(seq_len(length(p) - 1L),
                            \(i) if (.dag_has_edge(x, p[i], p[i + 1L])) " -> " else " <- ")
    paste0(p[1], paste0(steps, p[-1], collapse = ""))
  })
  open <- purrr::map_lgl(found, \(p) !.dag_path_blocked(x, p, Z))
  ord <- order(label, method = "radix")
  list(paths = label[ord], open = open[ord])
}

adjustmentSets <- .adjustment_sets_builtin
isAdjustmentSet <- .is_adjustment_set_builtin
paths <- .paths_builtin

# The figure, for a graph from either engine. Colour marks the exposure and
# the outcome. Each arrow stops at the edge of the box of its target.
.dag_parts <- function(d) {
  if (inherits(d, "dagitty")) {
    xy <- dagitty::coordinates(d)
    list(nodes = data.frame(name = names(xy$x), x = unname(xy$x), y = -unname(xy$y)),
         edges = dplyr::transmute(dagitty::edges(d), from = as.character(.data$v),
                                  to = as.character(.data$w)),
         exposure = dagitty::exposures(d), outcome = dagitty::outcomes(d),
         latent = dagitty::latents(d))
  } else {
    at <- \(v, k) if (v %in% names(.dag_xy)) .dag_xy[[v]][k] else NA_real_
    list(nodes = data.frame(name = d$nodes, x = purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) at(v, 1)),
                            y = purrr::map_dbl(d$nodes, \(v) at(v, 2))),
         edges = d$edges, exposure = d$exposure, outcome = d$outcome, latent = d$latent)
  }
}

plot_dag <- function(d) {
  parts <- .dag_parts(d)
  nodes <- parts$nodes |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      unplaced = is.na(.data$x),
      x = dplyr::if_else(.data$unplaced, 1.2 * (cumsum(.data$unplaced) - 1), .data$x),
      y = dplyr::if_else(.data$unplaced, -3, .data$y),
      half_w = 0.06 + 0.032 * nchar(.data$name),
      role = dplyr::case_when(.data$name %in% parts$exposure ~ "exposure",
                              .data$name %in% parts$outcome ~ "outcome",
                              .data$name %in% parts$latent ~ "unobserved",
                              .default = "observed"))
  # how far along a unit vector (ux, uy) the edge of a box of half-width w lies
  to_edge <- \(ux, uy, w) pmin(w / pmax(abs(ux), 1e-9), 0.15 / pmax(abs(uy), 1e-9))
  tails <- dplyr::select(nodes, from = "name", x0 = "x", y0 = "y", w0 = "half_w")
  heads <- dplyr::select(nodes, to = "name", x1 = "x", y1 = "y", w1 = "half_w")
  arrows <- parts$edges |>

                  uy = (.data$y1 - .data$y0) / .data$len,

    ggplot2::geom_segment(data = arrows, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),

    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.5)) +

`adjustmentSets()` returns the empty set `{}`: nothing in the graph causes the period in which a union began, so among all women the comparison of periods needs nothing held constant. The three paths between the period and marriage all run through `cohabits`, a common effect of the period, of education and of race-ethnicity (a collider), and without any conditioning they are closed. Keeping only cohabitors conditions on that collider and opens all three: among cohabitors, the period goes with education and race-ethnicity, because the mix of women who cohabit changed, as the shares above showed. ## Answers

1.  Under the selection alone, the arrow of the claim and the three paths through education and race-ethnicity are open; with education and race-ethnicity held constant, the arrow of the claim alone. The difference between the two comparisons is the change in who cohabits.
2.  A mediator: part of the change would run through a change in the age at which couples moved in, and holding it constant removes that part. In these data the mean age at the start was 22.0 in both cohorts, so the path carries little.
3.  No adjustment answers the claim about cohabitors as they were, the change in who cohabits included. Age, race-ethnicity and education answer it for cohabitors of the same characteristics, the change in behaviour within groups. Both are readings of "cohabitors" that a careful analyst could hold.

The three adjustment sets of the menu follow the graph: nothing besides the time since the start of the union (`"none"`), the age at the start and its square (`"age"`), and those with race-ethnicity and education, the controls of the paper without its interactions (`"composition"`). The adjustment set is the third argument of `try_spec()` in Task 4, and whatever you conclude here belongs in field 4 of your preregistration in Task 5.

d <- data[, c("OUTCOME", "P95", "P10")]
marry95 <- sum(d[d$P95 == 1 & d$OUTCOME == 2, ]$P95)
marry2010 <- sum(d[d$P10 == 1 & d$OUTCOME == 2, ]$P10)
total95 <- sum(d$P95)
total2010 <- sum(d$P10)
prop.test(x = c(marry95, marry2010), n = c(total95, total2010), correct = T)
```

You should get `X-squared = 47.474, df = 1`, the value on record for analyst 5X3KG, reproduced from the file of the analysts. Type your $\chi^2$ into the chat, hold it, and send it on the facilitator's word.
:::
::::

Now look at the two shares that the test compares. Of the 5,414 rows of 1995, 4 record a marriage; of the 18,535 rows of 2006–2010, 195. In this file the share of months that end in a marriage is fourteen times larger in the later survey, so cohabitors became *more* likely to marry, the opposite of the claim, and the analyst concluded exactly that.

An exact reproduction shows that the code and the file give the number on record. It does not show that the number is right. Run the next cell, which counts the unions of the file one by one, and the one after it, which asks whether each union of the paper is in the file.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}

data <- read.csv("data/score_person_months.csv")  # r-style: keep – readr is not loaded on this page

# One row per union: the outcome of each union is in its last row
score_unions <- data |>
  filter(P95 == 1 | P10 == 1) |>
  slice_max(MONTHNUM, n = 1, by = CASEID) |>
  mutate(survey = if_else(P95 == 1, "1995", "2006-2010"),
         outcome = c("intact", "marriage", "separation")[OUTCOME])
count(score_unions, survey, outcome)
```
:::



::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# Which of the 929 unions of 1995 in the window of the paper are in the file?
spec_unions(unions) |>
  filter(cycle == "1995") |>
  mutate(in_score_file = caseid %in% as.character(score_unions$CASEID)) |>
  count(outcome, in_score_file)
```
:::


The file holds **376 unions of 1995: 3 intact, 4 marriages and 369 separations**, where the paper has 929: 242, 340 and 347. Its 2006–2010 unions (446, 195 and 509) are close to the 1,142 of the paper. Of the 347 separations of 1995, 346 are in the file; of the 340 marriages, 2; of the 242 intact unions, 3. The [codebook](data/score_person_months_codebook.md) of the file explains why. SCORE took the length of each 1995 union from the date on which the woman stopped living with her first former partner, minus the date on which she began to. That date exists only for a union that dissolved, so the unions that became a marriage, or were still intact, fell out. Any comparison of the share of unions, or of months, that end in a marriage finds on this file that marriage became more common after 1995.

*Optional extension.* The same test on the file with its 1995 rows rebuilt from the 929 unions of the paper, written in the conventions of the file:


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}

rebuilt_1995 <- spec_unions(unions) |>
  filter(cycle == "1995") |>
  mutate(n_months = duration + (outcome != "intact")) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_months, .id = "MONTHNUM") |>
  transmute(OUTCOME = if_else(MONTHNUM == duration + 1, 2 * (outcome == "marriage") + 3 * (outcome == "separation"), 1),
            P95 = 1, P10 = 0)
rows_2010 <- data |>
  filter(P10 == 1) |>
  select(OUTCOME, P95, P10)
repaired <- bind_rows(rebuilt_1995, rows_2010)
prop.test(x = c(sum(repaired$P95 == 1 & repaired$OUTCOME == 2), sum(repaired$P10 == 1 & repaired$OUTCOME == 2)),
          n = c(sum(repaired$P95), sum(repaired$P10)))
```
:::


With the 1995 rows rebuilt the test gives $\chi^2$ = 87.68, and the share of months that end in a marriage is now *lower* in the later survey (1.1% against 2.4%), in the direction of the claim.

**The result that the claim quotes.** The second part of the task reproduces −0.683, the coefficient of Model 2, from the unions that the course rebuilt from the NSFG. Model 2 is a multinomial logit of marrying or separating against staying together, on person-months, weighted, with the age at the start and its square, the months since the start, race-ethnicity, education and the interaction of race-ethnicity and period, and with errors that follow the design of both surveys. It is not on the curve of Task 4, which is why `try_spec()` refuses it, but `fit_spec()`, the estimator that built the curve, fits it:


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
model_2 <- fit_spec(unions, adjust = "race_period")
model_2[, c("b", "se", "stat", "df", "n", "n_unions")]

# The reference specification of the curve: the same model without the
# interaction of race-ethnicity and period
reference <- fit_spec(unions)
reference[, c("b", "se", "stat", "df", "n", "n_unions")]
```
:::


Model 2 gives **−0.686 (SE 0.138)** against the published −0.683 (SE 0.14), on 33,197 rather than 54,291 person-months. The reference specification, the same model without the interaction, gives **−0.730 (SE 0.111)**. The gap between them is a matter of what the coefficient means. Beside an interaction of race-ethnicity and period, the coefficient of the period is the change for the reference group of race-ethnicity, non-Hispanic white women; the change for each other group adds its interaction:


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
b2 <- fit_model(unions, adjust = "race_period")$coef[, "marriage"]
round(c(white    = b2[["later"]],
        black    = b2[["later"]] + b2[["later_black"]],
        hispanic = b2[["later"]] + b2[["later_hispanic"]],
        other    = b2[["later"]] + b2[["later_other"]]), 2)
```
:::


The change is −0.69 for non-Hispanic white women, −0.40 for Black women, −1.14 for Hispanic women and −1.61 for the other group, which is small. The claim speaks of cohabitors, not of white cohabitors, so the reference specification of the curve leaves the interaction out and pools the change of all four groups: −0.730. The scripts that the analysts submitted are on the OSF, in the Multi100 component of the paper (osf.io/b69nv).

## Reproduction and the five analysts

In the workspace and on this page, everyone reproduces the recorded value exactly, because everyone runs the same code on the same file. This is why reproducibility is the cheapest of the three Rs to establish, and also why it settles so little: the file itself was wrong.

The five Multi100 analysts each wrote their own code for this claim. Two concluded that their results were evidence for it (73FDT and 456AP), two that they were evidence for the opposite (N8ZYW and 5X3KG), and one that they were evidence neither way (JDA15). Every analysis that used the 1995 rows met the faulty cohort, and one analyst saw it: "the data for 1995 in the OSF dataset seemed faulty, since there were only 4 marriages on record (in the paper 340 marriages were listed for 1995). I thus decided to exclude the 1995 data from the analysis." With the 1995 rows rebuilt, every analysis that uses them points the way of the claim: the logit of N8ZYW moves from z = +5.71 to −9.65, and that of JDA15 from z = −1.13 to −12.28. The disagreement that Multi100 recorded on this claim came from the file, not from the choices of the analysts. The [case study](index.qmd) sets out what each analyst chose.
:::

## Task 4 – The menu {#task-4-menu}

This task is **exploratory**. You try several specifications, look at what each one does, and get a feel for which choices move the estimate and which barely touch it. Nothing in this task is preregistered; the preregistration comes in Task 5.

`try_spec()` takes one argument per decision of the [specification menu](menu.qmd), and every argument defaults to the reference specification, the model of the paper without its interaction: the cohorts of the paper, every observed month, age, race-ethnicity and education held constant, weighted, the months since the start as a straight line, a multinomial logit. So changing one thing means changing one argument, and everything you do not name stays as it was. Every call is a live fit in your browser and takes about a second.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# Nothing changed – the reference specification.
try_spec()
```
:::


The printout gives the coefficient of the later cohort on the log scale with its 95% interval, the same result as a ratio of monthly chances, the *t* test with design-based errors (the rule that classes every point of the curve: errors computed from the strata and clusters of both surveys, as NCHS advises), the *z* of conventional errors for comparison, the person-months, unions and marriages analysed, the partial *r* by the conversion rule of Multi100, the class of the result, and its place among the 144 specifications on the curve of the claim.

## Exploratory and declared

Because you chose this specification after finding out what several specifications do, it lacks the guarantee that comes with a choice declared in a preregistration before its result is known: no one can rule out that it was chosen *because* of its result. This is something that we almost never know about published papers, unless their analysis was preregistered and every departure from the preregistration documented. In this course exploration is a natural step, and you also practise preregistering the analysis that you choose, so you submit twice, once here and once in Task 5.
:::

## Task 5 – The preregistration {#task-5-preregistration}

Preregistration means setting out your choice in a plan **before** you know what it does, which stops you from quietly picking the specification that happens to give the answer you wanted. On this page the plan is the preregistration cell below, and it binds mechanically as well: the session remembers the choices that you declare in that cell, and `run_spec()` and `report_result()` read them from there.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## A shortened preregistration

*Each numbered comment maps to a question in the OSF "Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org" (the eight-question short form). Because you are reanalysing data that already exist, field 2 also stands in for the prior-knowledge section of the secondary-data template (van den Akker et al. 2021) – the part that AsPredicted leaves out.*
:::

Make one choice on each decision of the [specification menu](menu.qmd), complete the dotted lines, then run the cell. The seven decisions at Level 1 fix the question that you are asking, the three at Level 2 fix how it is measured, and the five at Level 3 fix how it is estimated. The curve of 144 specifications keeps two or more options on six of these decisions and a single option on the other nine. An option that is not on the curve stops `prereg()` with the reason why, as it stops `try_spec()`.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# ============================================================================
# MY PREREGISTRATION – one specification, declared before seeing its result
# ============================================================================
# 1. The claim I am testing: .................................................
# 2. The data + what I already know: cohab_unions.csv (first premarital
#    cohabitations rebuilt from the NSFG, public domain); I know that the
#    reference specification gives -0.730, and what my exploration in Task 4
#    showed.
# 3. My one specification – one choice on each decision. An option that is
#    not on the curve of 144 stops prereg() with the reason why.

# Level 1 – Estimands (each of these changes what is being estimated)
my_comparison <- "1995_2006"      # 1995_2006 (NSFG 1995 against NSFG 2006-2010)
my_cohorts    <- "paper"          # paper | five_years
my_horizon    <- "five_years"     # five_years | three_years
my_outcome    <- "marriage"       # marriage  (the couple marry each other)
my_adjust     <- "composition"    # none | age | composition
my_weights    <- "weighted"       # weighted | unweighted
my_sample     <- "paper"          # paper     (women aged 15-44, first cohabitation before any marriage)

# Level 2 – Measurement (the same question, put to the data differently)
my_histories  <- "rebuilt"        # rebuilt   (union histories rebuilt from the dates of the NSFG)
my_education  <- "paper"          # paper     (four groups, as in Table 1 of the paper)
my_short      <- "drop"           # drop      (unions of less than a month left out)

# Level 3 – Estimation (the same question and measures, another fit)
my_unit       <- "person_months"  # person_months (one row per month in which a union could end)
my_time       <- "linear"         # linear | yearly
my_model      <- "mlogit"         # mlogit | logit | cloglog
my_errors     <- "design"         # design    (from the strata and clusters of both surveys)
my_scale      <- "log_ratio"      # log_ratio (the coefficient on the log scale)

# 4. Why this specification answers the claim, in one sentence grounded in
#    the causal graph of Task 2: .............................................
# 5. Supported if the estimate is below zero with p < .05 under design-based
#    errors; undermined if it is not significant or above zero. I will report
#    what I get.

my_spec <- prereg()   # checks every choice, prints your preregistration and keeps it
```
:::


The cell above, copied into your notes, is your preregistration record.
